title: Statics and Dynamics: A Case Study of Supplementing Traditional Lectures with High Impact Practices such as Multiple-Attempt-Testing and Project-Based-Homework
reason: Compares cohort grade distributions and class averages per test attempt across semesters (baseline 2019 vs 2023/2024); entry/exit MSLQ surveys only compared pre/post. No per-student Canvas measure is related to success or to a construct.

extraction.design: case study, cohort comparison across semesters + pre/post survey
extraction.n_quote: test was conducted with 81 students (n=81) voluntarily deciding to respond to both the entry and exit surveys.
extraction.population: Statics and Dynamics engineering undergraduates, University of Central Florida (several semesters; e.g. 177 in Summer 2024 Dynamics, 340 in Spring 2019 Statics baseline)
extraction.lms_indicators: Canvas-graded multiple-attempt test scores, aggregated by attempt (class level)
extraction.outcome_or_construct: grade distributions, pass and DFW rates; self-reported MSLQ SRL, self-efficacy, test anxiety (pre/post)
extraction.notes: n_quote refers to the survey subsample. Paired-sample correlations (e.g. SRL r=.667) are entry-exit stability of the same self-report scale, not indicator-outcome relations. Secondary NOREL. ASEE conference paper.
